input.title: Parse quoted CSV header names so quoted columns are recognised
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

In parseStatement, the header line is split with a plain lines[0].split(",") instead of splitFields(). A header written as "date","amount","description" therefore keeps its double quotes, so the required columns are not found by name, and assertShape throws errors.rowShape on the header at row 1.

Change: parse the header with splitFields(lines[0]) (then lower-case each name), so quoted and unquoted headers produce the same column names. Data rows already use splitFields.

claims.text:
Issue #4636 is triaged. I labelled it `bug` and opened draft pull request pr-32, and the comment is posted.

The cause is in `src/ingest/parser.ts`. `parseStatement` splits the header line with a plain `split(",")` instead of `splitFields()`, which the data rows already use. A header like `"date","amount","description"` keeps its quote characters, so the required columns are never found and the `errors.rowShape` error fires at row 1. The fix is to parse the header with `splitFields()`.

The maintainer's comment on the issue closes it as a duplicate of #4601. I did not close it, since the close decision belongs to a maintainer. The duplicate status is worth checking against #4601, since the bug is in the header parsing.

I did not run the test suite against pr-32.

related_maintainer.resolution: Fixed in #961: the first line of a statement is now split with splitFields in src/ingest/parser.ts, so quoted column names are read the same way as quoted fields.
